A camera is a helpful extra, but the manual tells you not to rely on it alone. Moving slowly and looking directly gives you time to stop if something appears in your path while you reverse. Before you open a door, check for approaching vehicles, motorcycles, bicyclists and pedestrians, and keep a door on the traffic side open only as long as loading or unloading needs. A handy way to remember them is that they climb in order: ten, twenty, thirty, fifty, from hydrant to crosswalk to signal to rail. Look for a legal parking space, one that is not near a hydrant, crosswalk, signal or crossing, and stop there instead. An unbelted occupant can die in a crash at speeds as low as twelve miles per hour, which is slower than many parking lot speeds.
